title: Introduce modular mesh for tokens: unify color, typography, spacing, and elevation
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Replace ad-hoc token fragments with a modular 'mesh' that maps color palettes, type scales, spacing/radius, and shadow elevations into a cohesive set that scales for dense tables and expressive charts. This ticket covers spec, token mapping, migration plan, and lightweight dev handoff artifacts.

Scope:
- Define primary/neutral/accent palettes with semantic aliases for surface, interactive, and critical states.
- Propose a compact and a roomy typography scale (4-step delta) to support dense rows and large headings.
- Rework spacing/radius tokens into a composable scale (base unit 4px, variable radius tokens for controls/cards).
- Rationalize elevation/shadow tokens with measurable luminance and contrast targets for both light/dark themes.
- Provide migration mappings and codemods for components: Button, TableRow, DataCard, ChartLegend.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Token spec doc published in Confluence with examples for each component pattern.
2) Figma library updated with token variables and a demo kit showcasing tables at 8, 12, 16px densities.
3) Two PRs: design token JSON + README; one codemod script stub for TableRow padding and elevation.
4) Accessibility checks: color contrast matrix passes AA for body text and WCAG 2.2 for interactive states.
5) Migration plan and rollout notes ready for Engineers and Platform (estimate of disruption and feature flags).

Out-of-scope: full refactor of every legacy page; deep performance optimizations to rendering internals (handled by ENG tickets).

Trade-offs and decisions to surface:
- We prefer a small token set that composes rather than many one-off tokens; may require slight visual shifts on some legacy UIs.
- Elevation will favor contrast over micro-shadow fidelity to ensure charts and tables remain legible when layered.

Deliverables:
- Confluence spec: /confluence/redwood/design/tokens/modular-mesh-2025
- Figma file: https://figma.com/file/Example/Redwood-Tokens-2025 (demo frames + component kit)
- Repo PRs: github.com/redwood/design-tokens PR #4123 (token spec), PR #4125 (codemod stub)
- Hand-off checklist for Engineers and QA

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (spec + design assets): 2 weeks. Phase 2 (engineer integration + codemod): 2-3 weeks. Phase 3 (canary rollout for console tables): 1 week, then full rollout behind feature flag.

Risks:
- Visual delta on customer-facing dashboards that rely on precise shadows; we'll include visual regression tests.
- Time required from platform/engineering to accept token shape; will lock minimal surface area for initial integration.
